reason: The narrative is told from an omniscient third-person perspective focused on prophetic and royal figures (Elijah, Elisha, King Ahaziah, and the king of Israel). While working people and regular folk appear in the text (servants, messengers, sons of the prophets, men of the city, youths), they function as secondary characters or objects of divine/prophetic action rather than as the primary perspective through which the story is told. The narrative centers on the deeds and words of the prophet Elijah and his successor Elisha, their interactions with kings and their courts, and God's will expressed through them—not on the daily experiences or viewpoints of ordinary working people.
